classification.difficultyReason: Apply the taught distinction between speed and signed velocity to identify the omitted negative-velocity equation and explain the correction.

content.prompt: Bob is asked to find when a particle has a speed of $2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. He solves $\dot{x}(t)=2$ and gets two solutions. However, there were actually three solutions. Explain what Bob did incorrectly and what he should have done instead.

answer.short: Bob found only times with velocity $+2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Since speed is $|\dot{x}(t)|$, he should solve both $\dot{x}(t)=2$ and $\dot{x}(t)=-2$.
answer.worked: Speed is the magnitude of velocity: $|\dot{x}(t)|=2$. Bob’s equation $\dot{x}(t)=2$ omits motion at $2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ in the negative direction. He should also solve $\dot{x}(t)=-2$ and combine the valid times from both equations.
